factors.title: Restrictions change access to stores
factors.short: PSBB began 10 April 2020 in Jakarta; essential retail was exempted.
factors.evidence: Jakarta announced PSBB from 10 April 2020 for an initial 14 days, extendable. Food, daily-needs retail, and logistics were among the sectors permitted to operate.
factors.implication: Movement restrictions limited access to physical stores, including grocery locations inside malls.
factors.limit: A dated regional policy, not a nationwide blanket store closure or a permanent rule through 2025. Its effect on each MPPA site is not quantified here.
factors.aqcd: Actionable and geographically specific; dates and initial duration are known. No before/after MPPA footfall series is available.

factors.title: Household spending moved into contraction
factors.short: Real household-consumption growth: +5.04% in 2019 versus −2.63% in 2020.
factors.evidence: Indonesia’s real household-consumption growth changed from +5.04% in 2019 to −2.63% in 2020, a decline of 7.67 percentage points.
factors.implication: Contracting household consumption weakened the spending environment for retailers.
factors.limit: Growth rates describe national real consumption, not MPPA sales, nominal grocery revenue, or the spending level falling by 7.67%.
factors.aqcd: Quantitative and comparable across years. National evidence is mapped to formats; it does not measure each format’s demand.
factors.sourceNote: Annual real growth · Bank Indonesia / BPS.

factors.title: Digital adoption became a permanent consumer habit
factors.short: e-Conomy SEA 2020: 37% of digital consumers were new, and 93% intend to continue post-pandemic.
factors.evidence: In Google, Temasek, and Bain’s 2020 study, 37% of Indonesian digital consumers adopted digital services during COVID-19, and 93% intend to continue post-pandemic.
factors.implication: Pandemic mobility curbs created permanent digital shopping habits, accelerating long-term consumer demand for online grocery ordering.
factors.limit: Consumer survey covering digital users across Indonesia; measures digital adoption rate and behavioral retention, not retail store profit margins.
factors.aqcd: Quantitative benchmark of consumer digital adoption and permanence in Indonesia during the New Normal (FY2020).

factors.title: Digital channels broaden grocery competition
factors.short: 2020 channels competed for access; Alfagift reported over 8m Android/iOS downloads.
factors.evidence: MPPA and several case competitors operated digital shopping or delivery channels in 2020. Their reports document different models; a membership app is distinguished from an ordering channel.
factors.implication: Apps, websites and messaging services expanded access to grocery ordering and delivery.
factors.limit: Reach measures differ: downloads, loyalty members and active store shoppers cannot be treated as active online buyers. Comparable channel profit is not established.
factors.aqcd: Dated 2020 report evidence maps technology to named retailers. MPPA’s channel coverage is quantified, but overlapping store counts cannot rank customer adoption or profitability.

factors.sourceNote: 2020 company reports and dated channel records.

factors.title: Food waste and resource efficiency
factors.short: Bappenas estimated 23–48 million tonnes of food loss and waste annually across 2000–2019.
factors.evidence: A Bappenas study released in 2021 estimated national food loss and waste at 23–48 million tonnes per year during 2000–2019.
factors.scope: Indonesia’s food supply chain, 2000–2019; study published in 2021.
factors.status: Food loss and waste in the food system
factors.implication: Perishable grocery stock can spoil before sale, wasting resources and purchase costs. For MPPA’s recovery, lower waste could protect margins and cash invested in inventory; company-specific savings require measurement.
factors.limit: The range covers the national food chain over two decades. It is neither MPPA’s waste nor a 2020 point estimate, and does not establish a new annual trend.
factors.aqcd: Quantitative context and a specific operational exposure. No comparable MPPA waste series is available, so AQCD coverage is incomplete.
factors.sourceNote: Bappenas, 2021 · National food chain, not MPPA’s waste rate.

selectionScope: Five factors connected to profitable sales and financial capacity: political, economic, social, technological and environmental. Food-waste response ideas remain on the Ideas Board for later evaluation.
